textbookBox.concept: Chapter 1 of the textbook revisits positive integers. A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself, and a composite number has more than two factors.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Chapter 1 of the textbook revisits positive integers. A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself, and a composite number has more than two factors.
beats.speakEn: Chapter 1 of the textbook revisits positive integers. A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself, and a composite number has more than two factors.

beats.en: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says: every composite number can be written as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique, apart from the order of the primes.
beats.speakEn: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says: every composite number can be written as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique, apart from the order of the primes.

beats.en: The theorem also says a number like 4 to the power n can never end in the digit 0, because its only prime factor is 2 and a number ending in 0 needs the prime 5 as well.
